U.S. Army veteran Greg Anderson on Wednesday condemned President Donald Trump and his MAGA hawks, calling America “the worldwide terrorist” during an appearance on “The Joe Rogan Experience.”

“I have arrived at a point where I truly believe the U.S. government is the worldwide terrorist,” said Anderson, who served in the Army’s 75th Ranger Regiment with 14 overseas deployments before pursuing a career in law enforcement. “I just really, truly believe that.”

Among the examples he used as proof was the U.S. airstrike on a girls’ school in Minab, Iran, that killed up to 175 people — most of them children under 12. A United Nations fact-finding mission has noted the strikes could be tantamount to war crimes.

Anderson argued Trump, who in July dismissed images of the aftermath as “AI-generated” and did not commit to releasing the results of an investigation, is “not taking any fucking accountability.” Rogan said the “darkest thought” is that the school was intentionally targeted.

“And us as Americans should have a problem with that,” said Anderson. “I’m so fucking sick of people saying collateral damage is part of war. It’s like, you got your MAGA hat on, you’re fat, you’re sitting on the couch — what do you know about warfare?”

He added, “You ever looked at dead kids? ’Cause I have, dude. And it should fucking affect you as a human being. And if it doesn’t, there’s something wrong with you. ‘Oh, but they’re little brown kids on the other side of the world.’ Yeah, they’re somebody’s fucking daughters.”

Anderson noted that he and Rogan both have daughters themselves, urging the podcaster to imagine what that kind of loss must feel like. He then decried the slew of MAGA loyalists who dismiss him over this anti-war stance as un-American — or as a “terrorist sympathizer.”

The veteran went as far as admitting that if his children were killed by a dismissive foreign government, he would become a terrorist himself, prompting Rogan to argue U.S. interventions in Iraq and Afghanistan have already proven to spur such cyclical violence.

Catch the bulk of the conversation starting at 2:14:42 below:

Rogan endorsed Trump in the 2024 election but has since decried his “horrific” deportations, “insane” immigration raids — and “terrifying” war on Iran. He skewered tech company Palantir earlier this year for calling for a military draft by stating plainly, “How about fuck you, you go?”

Anderson isn’t the only critic with a sizable platform to equate America’s wars with terrorism.

Progressive pundit Hasan Piker argued earlier this year that the airstrike in Minab was “an act of terror” and that the U.S. has “pound for pound” killed more people than al Qaeda ever has. He was condemned for the argument by critics from both sides of the political spectrum.

Anderson argued that the same pundits and politicians who condemn political violence also frequently support foreign entanglements “whenever they fucking want,” however, and help launder the very wars of choice that end up “killing fucking 150 girls at a school.”

“And people see it,” Anderson told Rogan. “And I’m here to tell you, Joe, every person I know that is a Delta Force operator, a Navy SEAL, an Army Ranger, a Green Beret — and I have hundreds of friends from those organizations — feels exactly how I feel.”
